stories.title: It's official: EU will force Google to share search data and open up AI on Android
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: The EU is mandating that Google open up its AI capabilities and share search data on the Android platform.
This regulatory action represents a significant shift in how major tech players operate within the European market.
Google has publicly expressed concerns that these required changes could negatively impact user privacy and security.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its focus on generative AI capabilities.
Key associated technologies include transformers and safetensors, placing it within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers architecture.
Indicates active community interest ('Trending') in this specific LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is a newly trending model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality model outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run on user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Google is better than Apple at playing the AI regulations game
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The EU has mandated that Google grant greater access to Android for its AI competitors.
This regulatory action forces Google to open up its Android ecosystem, despite prior resistance.
The news highlights the increasing regulatory pressure on major tech players regarding AI competition.

stories.title: Roblox will let people use AI to make games on their phone
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Roblox is integrating AI tools directly into its mobile application for game creation.
This move signals Roblox's significant embrace of generative AI technology within its ecosystem.
The feature raises concerns about potential content overload and quality control on the platform.

stories.title: xAI can’t deny Grok makes CSAM anymore. So it’s suing users.
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI is taking legal action against a user accused of generating CSAM using its Grok AI.
This marks the first lawsuit filed by xAI in response to misuse of its AI model.
The incident highlights ongoing and serious safety and misuse challenges associated with large language models.

stories.title: Fear of humanoid robots spurs human workers to strike at Hyundai auto factory
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Hyundai plans to deploy 25,000 Atlas humanoid robots.
The rollout of these robots is scheduled to begin in US factories in 2028.
The anticipated automation is causing labor unrest, with human workers threatening strikes.

stories.title: Now, even Russia's most elite hackers are using Clickfix to infect devices
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A specific social-engineering technique, 'Clickfix,' is now being employed by elite Russian hackers.
The technique was previously associated primarily with financially motivated cybercriminals.
The news indicates an escalation in the sophistication and actors involved in cyber threats.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds to critics of AI coding in Linux: "Fork it. Or just walk away."
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, creator of Linux, is publicly dismissing calls to ban AI coding tools within the Linux ecosystem.
Torvalds has adopted a firm stance, advising critics to either 'fork it' or disengage from the discussion.
This signals a significant philosophical debate regarding the integration and acceptance of generative AI in core open-source development.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are now capable of generating and submitting pull requests (PRs) to software projects.
The research analyzes a large dataset (25,264 PRs) from popular GitHub repositories to study project-level adoption.
The study focuses on how these tools are adopted and managed within the context of human-agent collaboration in software development.

stories.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
stories.author: Moslem Attar-Raouf
bullet_points: Traditional penetration testing is insufficient for AI-enabled systems.
Adversaries can now influence system behavior by targeting inputs (prompts, data, sensors) rather than just infrastructure.
The focus of security testing must shift from resource compromise to behavioral objective violation.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Investigates the project-level adoption and management of agentic coding tools in software development.
Analyzes a large dataset of 25,264 agent-generated Pull Requests (PRs) across 2,361 popular GitHub repositories.
Highlights the shift toward new forms of human-agent collaboration as AI tools gain the capability to submit code contributions.

stories.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
stories.author: binyu
bullet_points: The research focuses on scaling Zero RL to an extremely large model size (a trillion parameters).
The primary goal of this scaling is to achieve emergent reasoning capabilities in the AI model.
The announcement originates from Hacker News, suggesting a technical or research-heavy audience.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware setups.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM orchestration tools by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval.

stories.title: Fortnite is getting a bunch of AI-powered ‘personas’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Epic Games is integrating AI-powered personas into Fortnite experiences.
Creators will be able to publish content featuring these AI characters starting July 30th.
36 pre-made characters with consistent voices and personas are available for creators to use as NPCs.

stories.title: Netflix says around 300 titles used generative AI
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Netflix is integrating generative AI into its content production pipeline.
Approximately 300 titles have utilized generative AI, primarily during post-production.
The adoption aims to boost output quality while simultaneously reducing costs and increasing speed.

stories.title: Google is renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is rebranding its AI note-taking application from NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook.
The app will continue to function as a standalone product despite deeper integration with Gemini and Google Search.
The feature was initially revealed in May 2023 under the codename Project Tailwind.

stories.title: HP fined 1.4 billion rupees for “cartelization” of ink cartridges, toner, PCs
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: HP was fined 1.4 billion rupees for alleged 'cartelization' practices concerning its printing supplies.
The fine stems from concerns raised by resellers who threatened to switch to counterfeit products.
The case involves the control and pricing of ink cartridges, toner, and PCs.

stories.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
stories.author: Jie Li
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of current Human-AI interaction when Large Language Models (LLMs) make errors during complex reasoning.
Proposes 'Deep Interaction,' an efficient method designed to improve error correction and iterative refinement in LLM usage.
Aims to overcome the inefficiency of simple re-generation or manual step-flagging in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) workflows.

stories.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling
stories.author: Robert Ogburn
bullet_points: Addresses the critical industry need for rapid professional upskilling amidst massive workforce reskilling demands by 2030.
Proposes a novel, end-to-end framework that integrates AI acceleration across five stages of the learning lifecycle (acquisition, content development, teaching, etc.).
Aims to overcome limitations in current frameworks, which often only accelerate single stages and lack industry validation.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence the preservation of 'rank' across network depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms to maintain gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard expressive operations (matrix multiplications, nonlinear activations) inherently reduce network rank, which the architecture must counteract.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether improvements from agent optimization methods are cumulative (compound) over time.
Current reporting often treats optimization gains as one-shot, failing to simulate real-world, continuous deployment scenarios.
The research uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to test the viability of recursively optimizing agents as new failures or tasks emerge.

stories.title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current neural decoding models, which are restricted to supervised learning (SL) requiring paired behavioral labels.
The proposed method, MOJO (Masked autOencoder-based approach), leverages unlabelled neural data to improve generalizability.
Accurate neural decoders are crucial for advanced neurotechnologies like Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) and closed-loop experiments.

stories.title: MetaPerch: Learning from metadata for bioacoustics foundation models
stories.author: Jenny Hamer
bullet_points: The research introduces 'MetaPerch' to enhance bioacoustic foundation models by leveraging recording metadata.
It addresses the underutilized potential of readily available metadata (like location and time) in large citizen science datasets.
The work aims to improve species detection models beyond relying solely on raw audio supervision.

stories.title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
stories.author: Vanessa Smilansky
bullet_points: The research explores the utility of genomic foundation models (like Evo 2) for biosecurity screening.
The study uses minimal, frozen linear and attention probes on Evo 2 activations to detect biosecurity signals without fine-tuning the large model.
The probes demonstrated strong discriminatory power in detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in metagenomic data.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components affect the 'rank' of the network across depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms for preserving gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard expressive operations (matrix multiplication, nonlinear activations) inherently reduce network rank.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether improvements from agent-optimization methods compound over time.
Current evaluations often treat optimization gains as one-shot, failing to model real-world, recursive deployment scenarios.
The research uses Terminal-Bench 2.0 to test the stability and cumulative benefit of iterative optimization.

stories.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
stories.author: Ben Zhou
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Hindcast' to evaluate LLM forecasters by backtesting against prediction markets.
Two major leakage issues compromise standard backtesting for LLMs: retrieval models can access post-event reports, and training data increasingly contains future information.
The research highlights critical methodological flaws in current LLM forecasting evaluation, suggesting a need for robust testing protocols.

stories.title: Can an Old Dog Be Taught New Tricks? Taking LLMs Beyond Sentence Level Translation
stories.author: Alaina Brandt
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current machine translation systems treating translation as a sentence-by-sentence task.
It introduces PAT (Pragmatic Auto-Translator), a RAG-based system designed for whole-document, corpus-informed translation.
The system leverages context from comparable corpora (U.S. English and Latin American Spanish) guided by user specifications.

stories.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
stories.author: Frederic Bechet
bullet_points: Introduces DeepStress, a new framework designed to stress-test deep search agents.
Addresses the gap in research regarding the robustness of search agents when faced with poor-quality evidence.
Uses a controlled synthetic environment to manipulate the frequency of challenging evidence during testing.

stories.title: SPyCE: Skill-Policy Co-evolution for Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Weijie Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces SPyCE, a method for Skill-Policy Co-evolution in multimodal agents.
Addresses limitations in existing RL methods where policies must relearn tool-use patterns from scratch.
Proposes an approach that integrates memory-based experience with policy updates to absorb reusable patterns.

stories.title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: A Three-Stage Analysis of How SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Pre-, Intra-, and Post-CoT Calibration
stories.author: Xiaoyu Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how post-training methods (SFT, RL, OPD) affect the confidence calibration of Large Language Models (LLMs) during reasoning.
It introduces a novel three-stage calibration framework to analyze confidence across pre-, intra-, and post-Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation.
The study moves beyond simple final-answer accuracy to examine how training techniques reshape the model's internal uncertainty estimation.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds addressed the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the Linux kernel development process.
The discussion touches upon the integration and potential impact of AI tools in core operating system development.
This represents a niche but highly relevant discussion at the intersection of AI and foundational software engineering.
